original_question: Let S(t) = (1/pi) arg zeta(1/2 + it). Carneiro, Chandee, and Milinovich proved, under the Riemann Hypothesis, that |S(t)| <= (C0 + o(1)) log t / log log t with C0 = 1/4. Reduce the constant C0 in this estimate.
target_in_paper: Section "Bounds for L-functions", Problem 23: improve the Carneiro-Chandee-Milinovich RH bound for S(t) by reducing the constant 1/4 in |S(t)| <= (1/4 + o(1)) log t / log log t.

refined_question: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let S(t) = (1/pi) arg zeta(1/2 + it), with arg zeta defined in the standard way. Carneiro, Chandee, and Milinovich proved that |S(t)| <= (1/4 + o(1)) log t / log log t as t -> infinity. Can one lower the leading constant 1/4? Equivalently, prove that there exists a constant c < 1/4 such that, under RH, |S(t)| <= (c + o(1)) log t / log log t for all sufficiently large real t.
justification: The draft matches Problem 23 in the paper's section "Bounds for L-functions". It is not Problem 22, which concerns bounds for zeta(1/2+it) itself rather than S(t). The paper's official formulation is extremely brief, so your draft is already close; the main improvements needed are only to make the asymptotic quantifier and the meaning of the argument function fully explicit, while keeping the scope exactly at lowering the constant 1/4 in the RH bound for S(t).
